During phase II there was a shift toward food quality around 1970s in some European countries and in 1990s and 2000s in the
USA and the UK as a response to increased prevalence of diet-related diseases resulting from increased food availability. Many devel-
oped countries, including USA and most European countries, issued national dietary guidelines focusing in reducing energy levels
while increasing the number of nutrients per kilocalorie. This phase still continues as of today in many countries.
Phase III emerges since phase II seems unable to respond to individual (providing high-quality food to reduce all forms of
malnutrition) and societal (preserving the environment to do the same for future generations) challenges in a sustainable food
context. This phase is in its infancy in many countries coexisting with phase II. It aims at transforming SFPs in integrative learning
